newsitem.title: UK: Dollar likely to dominate soft oils in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar likely to dominate soft oils in Europe.

text.p: The dollar looks sets to dominate soft oils this week after lower Chicago soy futures early last week and U.S. currency strength squeezed already tight crush margins in Europe, traders said on Monday.
Chicago soyoil futures hit a four-year low last week after news that the USDA had pegged 1997 soybean acreage at the highest for 15 years.
However, the downside in Europe was limited by the stronger dollar.
"Crushers are finding it almost impossible to find a margin and they are calling the tune no matter what Chicago does," said one trader.

"If the dollar remains strong it is going to put a break on any downside movement, but on the other hand we have the highest soybean plantings for 15 years and near ideal growing conditions in the U.S.," said another trader.
Palm oil followed the trend in Chicago last week but traders said the market was trying to consolidate.
In his latest report Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong estimated local palm oil output during June at 785,000 tonnes against 790,640 in May.
However, exports were put at 595,000 tonnes against 626,606 during May.
"There is no fresh buying interest from any of the major buyers, and with soyoil looking as if it is going to come lower, palm oil will have to follow," said a trader.
There was little interest in the lauric oils sector with only light trading reported last week and with traders seeing no reason for the situation to change in the coming week.
Markets looked set to come down overall, but there was a warning over possible weather damage to crops.

Last week the independent Hamburg based publication Oil World said there was a 50 percent chance the U.S., Europe and Africa would be negatively affected by El Nino while there was a 60-80 percent chance of droughts in Oceania and Asia.
That would hit not only oilseeds production, but also palm oil.
